key_insight: Optimized gradient boosting predicts friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum joint strength with R² = 0.978 and identifies process windows targeting at least 90% joint efficiency.
engineering_relevance: The model provides a quantitative basis for selecting welding parameters, with shoulder plunge depth helping refine the high-strength process window.
method: Predict ultimate tensile strength from rotational speed, welding speed, and shoulder plunge depth.
Compare baseline models, then tune gradient boosting decision trees using grid search.
Use SHAP to interpret parameter effects and map predicted high-strength process windows.
evidence_signal: Using 27 experimental samples and leave-one-out cross-validation, reported R² increased from 0.905 for a decision tree to 0.966 for gradient boosting and 0.978 after tuning.
watch_item: The small dataset and lack of reported independent validation warrant experimental confirmation of predicted process windows before production use.
paper_title: Interpretable ensemble learning for tensile strength prediction and welding process window optimization of friction stir-welded 7N01 aluminum alloy
